disclaimer: Prey Chrov is a work of fiction. Its creatures, ruins, tablets and story are creative interpretations inspired by folklore, not authoritative descriptions of Khmer religion or culture. They will be reviewed with cultural advisors.

entries.text: In Khmer tradition, Neak Ta are respected guardian spirits of a place, honoured with shrines and offerings. In this game they are always benevolent protectors, never enemies.
In Khmer folklore, Ap is a feared night spirit. In this game it is a hostile creature of the dark, and an invention for play rather than a faithful portrayal.
Arak is a malevolent spirit in Khmer folk belief. Here it is a dangerous night enemy, loosely inspired and fictionalised.
A prasat is a Khmer temple tower or sanctuary, many of them sacred places still. The overgrown ruins in this game are imagined and do not depict any real site.
The krama is the everyday checked cotton scarf of Cambodia, used as a head covering, sling and more. In this game it is a nod to that practical, familiar cloth.
